2. Relevant facts, in short, are that the respondent No. 7, Manager, pubali Bank Ltd. as plaintiff instituted Artha Rin Case No.64 of 2005 before the Artha Rin Adalat, 3rd Court, Dhaka for realization of its outstanding dues amounting to Tk. 39,21,694.38. Ultimately, the suit was decreed ex-parte vide ex-party judgment and decree dated 7.6.2005 (decree signed on 16.6.2005). After obtaining the ex-prate judgment and decree the decree-holder-Bank put the decree into execution by filing Artha Jari Case No. 281 of 2005 before the Artha Ran Adalat, 3"1Court, Dhaka. 

 3. During the pendency of the said execution case the decree-holder-Bank on 20.11.2005 filed an application under section 34(1) of the AM, 2003 for issuance of warrant of arrest against the judgment-debtors. The Artha Rin Adalat upon considering the application by its order No.4 dated 20.11.2005 allowed the application and ordered to issue warrant of arrest against the judgment-debtors namely, Dr. Md. Abul Kalam and another. 

 5. Ms. Panda Akhter Chowdhury, the learned Advocate appearing for the judgment-debtor-petitioners at the very outset submit that she is not inclined to press first part of the Rule in much as by now it has been decided in so many cases by this court that the section 34 of the AM, 2003 is not ultra-vires the Constitution. She next submits that the Artha Rin Adalat under misconception of law and facts most illegally issued warrant of arrest by the impugned order dated 20.11.2005 and as such the same is liable to be struck down. She in the course of argument takes us through the sheets of the executing Court and the application under section 34(1) of the Ain, 2003 filed by the respondent Bank and then submits that admittedly the petitioners took loan by mortgaging huge shares of various companies namely, 1) Rangpur Foundry Ltd. 2) Tripti Industries (Bangla Road), 3) C:f.E. Vegetable, 4) Beximco pharma, 5) Glaxo well come, 6) Reokitt & Banckiser, 7)Perfume Ctc. (Manola) and 8) Samata Leather but the Bank  without taking any steps to sell those shares filed an application under section 34 of the Ain, 2003 praying for issuance of warrant of arrest. Referring to the provisions of section 34 of the Ain, 2003 the learned Advocate submits with force that section 34 of the Ain, 2003 empowers the Adalat to pass an order of warrant of arrest/civil imprisonment against the judgment debtor in complying the mandatory provision of section 34(9) of the Ain, 2003 and in this case the decree-holder—Bank could not or did not take any step to sell the pledge order share certificates and as such the impugned order of warrant of arrest is liable to be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and in of no legal effect. 

 7. We have heard the learned Advocates of both the sides at length, perused the writ petition, affidavit-in-opposition and other documents as filed thereto. To appreciate the submissions of the learned Advocates of both the sides, let us see first whether the decree-holder-Bank took any attempt to sell the pledge share certificates. 

 9. On our quarry, Mr. Nazmul Alam, the earned Advocate for the respondent-Bank admits that the decree-holder—Bank without taking any steps to sell the pledge share certificates filed an application under section 34(1) of the Ain, 2003 for issuance. of warrant of arrest against the judgment-debtors. He however, submits that the judgment-debtor-petitioners took loan depositing share certificates of 8(eight) companies but out of which only 3(three) Companies namely 1) Rangpur Foundry Ltd. Chittagong Ltd. 2) Citation Vegetable and 3) Beximco pharma are listed with Dhaka Stock Exchange.
